purpose: Testosterone undecanoate is used to treat men whose bodies do not make enough testosterone on their own, a condition called hypogonadism. It helps restore testosterone to normal levels. This can improve energy, sex drive, muscle strength, and mood in men with low testosterone.
how_it_works: Testosterone is a natural male hormone that your body normally makes. When your body does not produce enough, this medicine replaces it. It works just like your body's own testosterone, attaching to receptors in your cells to help them function normally and support male characteristics.
common_side_effects: Acne or oily skin, mood changes, increased red blood cell count, injection site pain or discomfort (for the injectable form), headache, increased or decreased sex drive, nausea, and swelling in the ankles or feet.
warnings: This medicine can increase your risk of blood clots, stroke, or heart attack, especially if you already have heart problems. It should not be used by women who are pregnant or may become pregnant, as it can harm an unborn baby. It may cause serious breathing problems called pulmonary oil microembolism right after an injection — this is why the injectable form must be given in a healthcare setting and you must be observed for at least 30 minutes afterward. It can also cause sleep apnea and may affect prostate health, so regular check-ups are important.
typical_dosing: The injectable form (Aveed) is given as a shot into the muscle by a healthcare provider — usually one injection every 10 weeks after the first two starter doses. The oral capsule form (Jatenzo) is taken by mouth twice a day with food, with the dose adjusted by your doctor based on your testosterone levels. Never adjust your dose on your own without talking to your doctor.
